# Toggle

A button that stays pressed or not.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toggle--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Toggle examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toggle--docs">Open Toggle in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toggle--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** One mode in the table toolbar that turns on and off. Not for settings saved at once, which use a switch.

- **Use it when:** Turning a mode or format on and off in a toolbar, such as bold.
- **Not when:** A setting saved at once (switch), or a one-off action (button).

Instead:

- [Switch](./switch.md): A setting.
- [Button](./button.md): A one-off action.
- [Toggle group](./toggle-group.md): Several toggles together.

## Why it works this way

Toggle looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toggle, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-content-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the main content?</b><code>content.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Numbers and records</div><p>Most of the screen is numbers and records.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: In the table toolbar, with no border; the pressed state shows as a fill, quiet beside the data.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>outline</b>: Borders on every toggle would compete with the data.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Badge: neutral</code> <code>Badge: info</code> <code>Badge: success</code> <code>Badge: warning</code> <code>Badge: danger</code> <code>Sidebar: default</code> <code>Sidebar: outline</code> <code>Empty: default</code> <code>Item: default</code> <code>Item: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">5</div><small>Toggle decisions would reopen</small><p>and 44 answers that follow from it: <b>A lot</b>, <b>Scan and compare</b>, <b>People keep their place</b>, and 41 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How often do people repeat actions?</b><code>tasks.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Constantly</div><p>The same actions repeat many times an hour.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: In the table toolbar, with no border; the pressed state shows as a fill, quiet beside the data.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: ghost</code> <code>Input group: inline-end</code> <code>Sidebar: default</code> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Toast: success</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toggle decision would reopen</small><p>and 11 answers that follow from it: <b>Time on task</b>, <b>All day</b>, <b>Three</b>, and 8 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-content-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How much is on one screen?</b><code>content.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">A lot</div><p>Experts want many records on one screen.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: Toggles sit in the table toolbar, at the smaller size like compact buttons.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>sm</b>: The table toolbar, matching compact buttons. It still fits a mouse.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>lg</b>: Controls stay small so more records fit on one screen.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: default</code> <code>Button: compact</code> <code>Button: large</code> <code>Input group: block-start</code> <code>Input group: block-end</code> <code>Field: horizontal</code> <code>Sidebar: lg</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Toggle decisions would reopen</small><p>and 14 answers that follow from it: <b>Quiet</b>, <b>Only the steps the screens need</b>, <b>Small</b>, and 11 more.</p></div></div></section>

It still fits a mouse.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: default</code> <code>Button: compact</code> <code>Item: sm</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toggle decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Space or Enter presses it. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It says whether it is pressed. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toggle
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
